_description: Named risk-profile overrides for config.json — the four-tier risk LADDER, applied by /set-risk-profile. See docs/risk-profiles.md for the full design rationale (what the ladder's axis is, why its thresholds are profile-relative, and why trade count is deliberately not a ladder dimension), and GATES.md for the gate-by-gate catalog.
_ladder_note: The ladder is the ONLY profile registry now. Its axis is RISKIER TRADES, not more trades: climbing a rung loosens entry quality (IV floor, credit floor, short-call delta, OTM distance) and is offset by fewer concurrent positions and a tighter stop. Trade count is therefore flat across rungs (daily_ic_trade_target = 2 everywhere, always <= max_concurrent_ics). Thresholds that used to be shared absolutes are now derived per profile from its own min_iv_rank and credit floor (low_iv_credit_floor_iv_rank_offset, low_iv_credit_relief_multiple, late_entry_bias_iv_rank_offset in config.json) — a shared absolute silently flattened the ladder, see docs/risk-profiles.md. In reporting, one PORTFOLIO is formed per (profile x symbol) pair, each with its own max_concurrent_ics and daily-target budget.
_removed_note: The 15 symbol/wing/credit experiment cells (small-/medium-/large-/explore-) were removed on 2026-07-18 pending a rethink; they are recoverable from git history. They pinned a symbol and wing per cell, which conflicted with the (profile x symbol) portfolio model where the symbol is its own axis. Re-introduce them as symbol-agnostic branches if the study resumes.
_width_study_note: WIDTH STUDY (2026-07-28): the four width-* profiles are forced-sampling experiment arms, the retired-cells study resumed in the symbol-agnostic form docs/paper-experiments.md prescribes. Each fixed arm differs from its siblings in EXACTLY one variable (the wing width); width-adaptive shares every sampling key and differs only in offering all three widths with the widest-first fee-drag-bias policy -- the paired policy-vs-fixed comparison. All arms: stagger_entries makes daily_ic_trade_target a HARD cap (24 > the 20 possible 15-min ticks in the 09:30-14:30 paper window, so it never binds) and skips the over-target floor tightening, so every sample faces the same gate; max_concurrent_ics 99 means each trade stands alone (a sample stream, not a book); NO symbols key -- the (profile x symbol) grain gives width-N:XSP and width-N:QQQ cells automatically. Regime gates (VIX/ATR/GEX) inherit from base config so every arm blocks at the same ticks and the pairing survives. conservative remains a REFERENCE curve only (different sampling semantics). Names use '-' not ':' (portfolio keys are prof:symbol). Read results per docs/paper-experiments.md's width-study section: true pairs first, divergence log second, per-cell streams third; same-day trades are clustered.

conservative._note: Default: today's settings. Strict IV/credit floors, wide OTM buffers, latest entry time (12:00 PM). Fewest trades (~1–2/day), highest per-trade safety margin. Best for learning, uncertain markets, or recovery after losses.

moderate._note: Tier 1: Relax IV-rank (0.22) and credit floors (0.12), enter earlier (11:00 AM), tighten stop to 0.93 to offset. ~1 more trade/day vs conservative, thinner per-trade credit margin but paired with tighter stop. Use after 2–4 weeks on conservative if entry rejections are high.

aggressive._note: Tier 2: Tier 1 + accept tighter OTM strikes (delta 0.22, calls 0.30% OTM, puts 0.25% OTM); offset with max_concurrent_ics=3 (25% fewer positions) and stop_trigger_ratio=0.90 (5% tighter than conservative). ~2–3 more trades/week, each one riskier but total exposure capped. Requires active stop management. Use after 2+ weeks on moderate with 60%+ win rate.

very-aggressive._note: Tier 3: Tier 2 + regime gates relaxed (VIX pause at 30, ATR pause at 40); trade through higher-vol/trending conditions. Tightest offsets: max_concurrent_ics=2 (50% fewer), stop_trigger_ratio=0.85 (10% tighter than conservative). Highest activity (~3–5 more trades/week on active weeks), highest per-trade risk. FOR DELIBERATE SHORT EXPERIMENTS ONLY — test high-VIX/ATR tactics for 1 week with explicit drawdown limits. Not a permanent trading mode.
very-aggressive._disabled_note: DISABLED 2026-07-27 on paper evidence — kept here rather than deleted so the rung can be re-enabled for a deliberate experiment. Over 9 sessions (07-10..07-27) it was the worst rung by a wide margin: -$1,668.11 across 45 trades (-$37.07/trade) against conservative's +$216.32 across 34 (+$6.36/trade), with the ladder monotonic in between. In a joint counterfactual over the whole 212-trade book, removing it was the single largest marginal improvement of any filter tested (+$604 on top of a correlated-symbol filter) — and unlike the symbol-level filters that result does not rest on one outlier session. Re-enable only for a time-boxed experiment with a stated drawdown limit, per the note above.

width-2._note: Width study, fixed arm: every entry is pinned to a 2-wide IC regardless of what the floor would otherwise pick. Forced-sampling: 15-minute spacing, no concurrency cap (99), each structure lives and dies on its own -- a sample stream, not a book. Paired against width-5/width-10/width-adaptive on the same tick.

width-5._note: Width study, fixed arm: every entry is pinned to a 5-wide IC regardless of what the floor would otherwise pick. Forced-sampling: 15-minute spacing, no concurrency cap (99), each structure lives and dies on its own -- a sample stream, not a book. Paired against width-2/width-10/width-adaptive on the same tick.

width-10._note: Width study, fixed arm: every entry is pinned to a 10-wide IC regardless of what the floor would otherwise pick. Forced-sampling: 15-minute spacing, no concurrency cap (99), each structure lives and dies on its own -- a sample stream, not a book. Paired against width-2/width-5/width-adaptive on the same tick.

width-adaptive._note: Width study, policy arm: offers 2/5/10 and picks the WIDEST that clears the credit floor (the fee-drag-bias policy), same forced-sampling cadence as the fixed arms. The paired policy-vs-fixed comparison -- same gates, same spacing, dynamic width per tick instead of a pin.
